title: Episode Review — Cariboo Signals, September 3, 2026
content_html:
What the pipeline did, what broke, and what it chose when something broke. Run 33736913709.

Two runs, one success: Gemini multi-speaker failed on the preamble

The 09:05 run completed successfully after the 08:05 run failed. At 09:30, episode 219 shipped to RSS. A third run began at 10:05 and is still in progress.

During audio render, Gemini's multi-speaker model rejected the preamble section with a finish reason of OTHER and returned no audio despite accepting the prompt. The pipeline fell back to single-speaker Gemini for four attempts. All four either rejected or returned silence. The remaining sections and credits rendered with OpenAI instead. Nothing was dropped from the episode—the voice split changed mid-episode, not mid-sentence.

Article body enrichment hit its budget

The Brave body-backfill service made 12 calls and exhausted its budget. Fifty-six roundup articles were dropped from the script. The remaining thin articles kept their stub bodies and stayed in the episode; they may be cut later if they remain sparse enough.

This is a cascade choice, not a failure. The pipeline prioritized depth over breadth. What shipped was shorter source text, not missing sources.

Script undershot, then corrected

The first draft arrived at 2,617 words against a 3,400-word target. The script was sent back for an expand pass. The final shipped version landed at 3,038 words—still 362 words short of target, but acceptable enough to publish.

Citation alignment tilted toward the roundup

Fourteen of fifteen roundup citations matched their sources. Two of three deep-dive citations matched. The three deep dives were:

  • Google battery technology deployment
  • Barclays infrastructure financing complaint
  • Workplace ostracism and productivity

One deep-dive source failed to match. The roundup held stronger.

Audio render took longest; TTS had one segment retry

Render episode audio consumed 529 seconds. Generate episode script took 481 seconds. One TTS segment came back shorter than word count predicted and was retried. The retry was also short. The longer of the two takes was kept, adding no gaps to the episode.

Final audio: 19.2 minutes, 17.6 MB. Video: 19.2 minutes, 55.4 MB.

Debate question and quality metrics

The episode centered on who controls infrastructure decision-making on Indigenous lands: whether self-sufficiency alone is sufficient, or whether contractual terms and connection quality matter more.

Quality checks found one AI-tell pattern hit. Voice ratio favored Casey at 1.06 to Riley. Three deep dives aired. Claude made 8 API calls consuming 88,500 input tokens.

title: Episode Review — Cariboo Signals, September 2, 2026
content_html:
What the pipeline did, what broke, and what it chose when something broke. Run 33606878277.

Gemini TTS failed twice; the pipeline fell back to OpenAI for most of the episode

The Gemini 3.1 Flash text-to-speech preview model timed out on the preamble section during canary testing. Both attempts hit a 45-second read timeout at generativelanguage.googleapis.com. The pipeline caught the failure and re-rendered the preamble plus all remaining sections and credits on OpenAI instead.

This is a clean fallback. The listener hears a complete episode with no gaps. What changed: Casey's voice carries 0.89 of Riley's screen time instead of a split designed around Gemini's multi-speaker capability. The episode shipped as planned, but not as architected.

Brave ran out of budget mid-roundup; thin articles lost their bodies

The pipeline made 12 Brave API calls to backfill article summaries before exhausting its allocation. Twenty-two articles that remained in the roundup kept only stub bodies. The system logged this once but repeated the note 22 times in the degradation list—one budget event with a cascading effect, not 22 separate failures.

The roundup still shipped 55 articles dropped and three deep dives included. Citation alignment tells part of the story: 14 of 15 roundup citations matched their sources, but zero of three deep-dive citations did. The deep dives came from TechRadar but carried no body text to verify against.

Script came in short, expanded once, and landed 115 words under target

The first draft reached 2,986 words against a 3,400-word target. The expand pass ran. The shipped script is 2,871 words—29 words shorter than the first draft and 529 words short of target. The label states that quality.script_words is what ran through audio synthesis, so this is the episode that aired.

The AI tell-pattern filter flagged 2 instances in the final script. The audio runs 17.8 minutes and the video 17.8 minutes, matching exactly.

Manual triggers ran fast; a fallback job five hours late sat pending

Three manual workflow dispatches completed cleanly between 08:05 and 10:09 UTC on September 2nd. The fourth run, a fallback trigger labeled "Fallback 2 (3:05 AM Pacific)," launched at 15:02 UTC—297 minutes behind schedule—and remained in-progress at the time this review was written.

Debate prompt centered on self-sufficiency versus institutional channels for security

The episode framed the question: should households and small businesses build their own technical defenses or rely on networks and formal channels? The debate anchored three deep dives on Geekom mini-PC malware, dead-site exploitation, and Google passkey theft.

93,492 Claude input tokens across 8 API calls plus 2 Brave-Answers calls. Episode 218 in the RSS feed. Final audio is 16.3 MB, video is 50.4 MB. Total wall time for script generation and audio rendering: 818 seconds and 632 seconds respectively.

What the pipeline did, what broke, and what it chose when something broke. Run 33485277361.

Gemini's TTS pipeline failed mid-episode; OpenAI finished the render

The news section audio was synthesized on Gemini's multi-speaker model when a connection timeout occurred after 120 seconds. The pipeline fell back to OpenAI for the remaining sections and credits. Two earlier canary checks against Gemini also timed out at 45 seconds, signaling a pattern rather than a glitch.

The listener hears this as a delivery inconsistency: Casey and Riley's voices (ratio 0.68 Casey to Riley) in the news segment may differ in timbre or pacing from the rest of the episode, which used a different provider.

Budget for article enrichment ran dry; 48 stories got dropped

The pipeline spent its 12-call budget for Brave body-backfill—a step that fills in thin article summaries to make them scriptable. When the budget was exhausted, remaining articles with stub bodies stayed sparse. The system dropped 48 roundup items rather than script them as fragments.

This explains the gap between source volume and what shaped the final script. The episode aired with 3 deep dives and an implicit selection bias toward fuller coverage.

Script expanded after undershooting target; citations held up

The first draft came in at 2,379 words against a 3,400-word target. The pipeline sent it back for expansion. The shipped script settled at 3,291 words—9 words short of target, but within acceptable bounds.

Citation alignment was strong: 14 of 15 roundup citations matched their sources (93%), and 2 of 3 deep-dive citations matched (67%). The unmatched deep-dive citation remains unresolved.

One TTS segment returned shorter than predicted

A single take came back with audio duration shorter than its word count suggested. The pipeline retried it once. No further action was needed.

Episode shipped at 20.8 minutes; three manual runs plus a stalled fallback

The audio file is 19.1 MB, video is 59.6 MB at matching duration. The episode was published to RSS as entry 217.

Three manual workflow runs completed successfully on 1 September between 08:05 and 10:09 UTC. A fourth run—Fallback 2, triggered at 3:05 AM Pacific—was created at 15:26 UTC, 321 minutes late. It remains in progress with no conclusion.

Today's frame: "Who actually gets to own the data and monitoring infrastructure that proves a mine is safe, and does legal standing to say no to development translate into independent technical capacity to verify environmental claims?"

title: Episode Review — Cariboo Signals, August 31, 2026
content_html:
What the pipeline did, what broke, and what it chose when something broke. Run 33393581627.

Gemini's spend cap forced a TTS fallback mid-pipeline

The Gemini project on this pipeline hit its monthly spend cap before rendering began. The system had a fallback ready: use OpenAI instead. But there was a second problem. Gemini's text-to-speech service failed its pre-flight check, so the pipeline could not risk switching voices mid-episode. The entire 18.7-minute episode rendered on OpenAI TTS to keep the voice consistent.

This is the constraint that matters: not money, but the technical requirement that a voice cannot change between segments. Gemini's failure made the fallback mandatory, not optional.

Script came short, expanded, then shipped under target anyway

The first draft hit 2,733 words against a 3,400-word target. The pipeline sent it back for an expand pass. The result was 3,059 words. That is 341 words short of the target, but it shipped. No second expand was attempted.

The shipped script also drew one hit on the AI tell pattern detector. The voice ratio between Casey and Riley was 0.89, meaning Casey carried slightly more of the episode.

Citation alignment broke on the deep dives

The roundup matched 12 of 15 citations. The deep dives matched zero of three. The pipeline pulled three stories: Australia's ban on fully AI-made songs in charts, press freedom in rebel-controlled eastern DRC, and a brutalist LA office conversion. None of their citations were verifiable against the script.

This is also where a Brave search limit became visible. The pipeline had a usage cap of 402 requests. It hit that limit mid-run. Every remaining Brave search was skipped. The anchor script had no per-weekday framings for the debate question either—each day frames it without preparation.

Three production runs, all late, one still running

The first run was manual and 163 minutes late. Three fallback runs followed, each triggered at 3:05 AM Pacific, each arriving 361 to 445 minutes late. The fourth is still in progress. All three completed runs reported success.

Audio and video specs

The episode is 18.7 minutes in both audio and video. Audio file is 17.1 MB. Video file is 53.7 MB. This brings the RSS feed to 216 episodes total.

One TTS segment came back shorter than its word count predicted. It was retried once. The retry was also short. The longer of the two takes was kept, so nothing was dropped from the episode.

Token spend and service calls

The pipeline made 11 calls to Claude and 2 calls to Brave Answers. Total input tokens to Claude: 88,811.

What the pipeline did, what broke, and what it chose when something broke. Run 33255914006.

Gemini TTS failed pre-flight; OpenAI rendered the whole episode

Four rate-limit errors from Gemini's text-to-speech models triggered the canary check to fail. The pipeline did not attempt a mid-episode voice switch. Instead, it fell back to OpenAI and rendered all 18.6 minutes of audio on a single vendor. The listener heard no interruption. The cost was vendor concentration for one day.

Brave Answers API hit its usage limit mid-run

The Answers API returned a 402 error. The pipeline switched to web snippets for the remainder of script generation. This affected the script/brave-answers segment. The first draft still arrived at 2,252 words, below the 3,400-word target, and was sent for an expand pass. The final script shipped at 2,955 words.

Ten roundup stories stayed out of order after one repair

A sorting failure in script/roundup-order left 10 stories aired after a later block, even after one correction attempt. The pipeline did not retry. Fifteen roundup stories were dropped from the episode entirely. Five deep dives ran instead.

Citation matching fell unevenly across segments

Roundup citations aligned at 13 of 15 matched. Deep dive citations aligned at 2 of 5 matched. The disparity tracks with the segment's relative complexity—the roundup used shorter, more predictable source text. The deep dives included pieces titled "B.C.'s Sikh community on edge after Edmonton attack" and "Artists Commit to the Bit at This Year's Vulva Gala," which required more precise extraction logic.

Three runs, each later than the last

The first completed run arrived 222 minutes late. The second completed 246 minutes late. A third began 293 minutes late and was still in progress at report time. All three triggered on Fallback 2, the 3:05 AM Pacific schedule. The repeating trigger and escalating latency suggest the primary schedule did not complete.

Script generation took 450 seconds; audio took 334

Generation was the slowest step in the pipeline by a margin of 116 seconds over audio rendering. The script required one expand pass after arriving under target. title: Episode Review — Cariboo Signals, August 28, 2026
content_html:
What the pipeline did, what broke, and what it chose when something broke. Run 33174274745.

Three runs to ship one episode

The pipeline triggered manually at 13:11 UTC and finished at 13:48 UTC, 186 minutes late. That run succeeded. Two hours later, the system fell back to its 3:05 AM Pacific trigger and ran again, 604 minutes behind schedule. It succeeded. At 20:43 UTC it ran a third time, 638 minutes late, and succeeded again. A fourth fallback started at 21:09 UTC and was still in progress when this review was written.

The facts do not state which run's output shipped to RSS (episode 213 published). The pattern suggests the first manual run was the intended delivery and the fallbacks were safeguards, but the review does not confirm this.

Answers API hit its usage ceiling mid-script

The script generation process has a segment called script/brave-answers that draws from Brave's Answers API. During this run, that API returned a 402 error with an "Usage limit exceeded" response. The pipeline switched to web snippets for the remainder of the script and continued.

This is a graceful fallback—the episode still aired with sourced material—but it represents a hard boundary. When the budget exhausts, the pipeline has no option to wait or retry at a different time. It downgrades and moves forward.

Citation matching broke down in the deep dives

The roundup section matched 13 of 15 citations to their sources. The deep dive section matched 2 of 3. The three deep dive stories were from APTN News, Forbes Innovation, and Vancouver Sun; the data does not show which source failed to align or why.

This gap is small in volume but structural. Roundup citations (news briefs) traced back reliably. Longer-form analysis did not. The pipeline will need to examine whether the matching logic scales to deeper reporting or if these segments need different handling.

Welcome section fell over to OpenAI mid-render

The audio render began using Gemini's multi-speaker text-to-speech for the welcome section. The connection timed out after 120 seconds. The pipeline fell back to OpenAI for that section and all following sections and credits.

The episode is therefore a seam: welcome came from one voice provider, the body and outro from another. The video file is 50.2 MB and 17.7 minutes long. The audio is 16.2 MB and the same 17.7 minutes. Listeners heard both, but not from a single synthesis engine.

Script needed one expansion cycle

The first draft arrived at 1,930 words against a 3,400-word target. The pipeline sent it back for expansion. The shipped script was 2,904 words—still 496 words short of target, but within acceptable range. This is documented as quality control, not failure; the expansion pass was the intended remedy for undershoot.

Voice balance and quality markers

Casey's airtime was 88% of Riley's. The script contained zero matches for tell-pattern detection (a quality filter for weak exposition). Two short TTS segments took back less audio than their word counts predicted; each was retried once and included in the final episode.

The debate question was: "Who should have the authority to act on their land during wildfires—individual property owners making real-time decisions, or government agencies issuing formal evacuation orders?" The pipeline generated 3 deep dives and processed 15 story candidates for roundup, of which 15 were dropped (none aired).

Pipeline and compute costs

Claude processed 92,818 input tokens across 12 API calls. Total script generation took 722 seconds; audio render took 618 seconds; deployment to GitHub Pages took 408 seconds. The video upload to YouTube took 67 seconds.

title: Episode Review — Cariboo Signals, August 22, 2026
content_html:
What the pipeline did, what broke, and what it chose when something broke. Run 32562874398.

Gemini's voice failed mid-pipeline, so the whole episode ran on OpenAI instead

The Gemini text-to-speech service timed out during pre-flight checks. Rather than risk a voice switch mid-episode, the pipeline fell back to OpenAI for the complete render. This is the correct failure mode—18.4 minutes of continuous audio demands a single voice—but it means the episode cost more than planned. The spend data shows Claude at 8 units; the full OpenAI render added to that total.

The timeout itself is tracked: Gemini's generativelanguage.googleapis.com endpoint returned read timeouts on multiple canary checks. This is infrastructure fragility, not a code problem. The system detected it before publishing and chose safety over economy.

Brave Search broke on three separate queries

The Brave API returned 400 errors on three research queries, all malformed requests according to the logs. Two involved the Bald Range wildfire story; one targeted Aurora Borealis content from Atlas Obscura. The pipeline did not retry these or mark them as fallback triggers. They simply failed and the episode moved forward without them.

Short-segment TTS had a 78% failure rate

Nine short audio segments were queued for text-to-speech synthesis. Seven failed and could not be recovered. The pipeline retried but did not escalate; these segments likely dropped from the final mix. This is a secondary degradation—the main episode rendered successfully—but it represents missing content downstream of the primary voice work.

38 roundup items were culled; 5 deep dives made it through

The pipeline dropped 38 candidate stories from the daily roundup. Five deep-dive pieces survived the curation gate: a cycling training ride in the Cariboo, B.C. lumber trade relief, ranching families west of Williams Lake (two Tribune stories), and Tyson Foods beef plant closures tied to drought. Citation alignment data shows 8 sources in the first tier, 15 in the second, none in the third, and 5 scattered elsewhere—an uneven distribution that suggests some sources clustered heavily while others appeared once.

The episode landed on the central question about regional economic power

Today's debate framing: "Does the Cariboo region have meaningful formal input into economic decisions made at federal and provincial levels, or does it only absorb outcomes determined elsewhere?" The deep dives anchor this—trade deals, closures, drought impacts, and local initiatives all touch the question of who decides and who adapts.

The run timeline: three attempts, all late

Primary run triggered at 1:05 AM Pacific, arrived at 1:39 AM (34 minutes late). Fallback 1 at 2:05 AM, arrived at 2:25 AM (20 minutes late). Fallback 2 at 3:05 AM began at 3:30 AM (25 minutes late) and was still in progress at report time. The primary and first fallback both completed successfully. Script generation took 11.5 minutes of the primary run's total 27.6 minutes; rendering and deployment consumed the rest.

title: Episode Review — Cariboo Signals, August 21, 2026
content_html:
What the pipeline did, what broke, and what it chose when something broke. Run 32465099342.

Gemini's timeout forced a full OpenAI render

The primary run started 46 minutes late and completed successfully, but not on the system it was built for. Gemini's text-to-speech canary failed twice with read timeouts against generativelanguage.googleapis.com. Rather than risk a mid-episode voice swap, the pipeline fell back to OpenAI for the entire audio render.

This was the correct choice operationally. The episode still delivered: 20.2 minutes of audio, 18.5 MB, published to the RSS feed at position 206. But it consumed Gemini's allocation without producing audio, then spent Claude tokens (7 of them) on script generation while OpenAI handled the voice work. The cost split reflects a pipeline forced to choose between reliability and its preferred vendor.

Brave search broke on two knowledge queries

Both Brave API calls returned 400 errors: one for Meshtastic version 2.8 features, another for salmon recovery funding by BC watershed. These were not timeouts or rate limits—the requests were malformed at the API level, suggesting either a breaking change in Brave's endpoint or a schema mismatch in how the pipeline constructs its queries.

The pipeline does not record whether these queries were skipped, replaced with cached results, or degraded to a fallback source. The episode completed, so the knowledge gaps were absorbed somewhere. Worth investigating whether Brave's chat endpoint has shifted its request contract.

Short-form script lengths diverged sharply

Two short-form scripts generated at 2467 and 3400 characters—a 38% spread. Without target lengths in the facts, it is unclear whether this reflects actual variation in source material or a drift in the generation prompt. Either way, both completed and both integrated into the episode.

Eight TTS segments failed retry and were skipped

The pipeline attempted text-to-speech on eight short segments and failed on all eight retries. These segments do not appear in the final audio. No error details are logged for the initial failures or the retries, so the cause remains opaque—whether they were malformed input, API rejections, or timeout cascades.

Citation alignment was poor

Four citation checks returned scores of 5, 15, 1, and 3 out of an apparent ceiling of 10 or 100. The three deep-dive sources (Turkish drones, salmon habitat recovery, Appalachian Trail tragedy) did make it into the episode, but their integration with the script ranked weak. This suggests the sources were used but not woven tightly to their claims.

Two fallback runs both succeeded within 31 minutes

The primary run was 46 minutes late. Two fallback triggers fired at 2:05 AM and 3:05 AM Pacific, each completing in under eight seconds of wall time. A third fallback (3:05 AM) was still in progress at report time. The redundancy worked: the episode published despite the primary delay.

title: Episode Review — Cariboo Signals, August 20, 2026
content_html:
What the pipeline did, what broke, and what it chose when something broke. Run 32350746969.

Gemini voice service failed twice; the pipeline rendered audio on OpenAI instead

The canary deployment for Gemini TTS timed out on two separate attempts. Both the wildcard test and the gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts instance hit 30-second read timeouts against generativelanguage.googleapis.com. Rather than risk a mid-episode voice switch, the pipeline downgraded to OpenAI for the entire 19.5-minute episode.

This choice preserved continuity at a cost. The spend line shows Claude consumed $10 of the budget while Gemini did not run. The audio rendered at 17.9 MB across 19.5 minutes—standard dimensions—but the listener heard a voice they may not have expected on a day when Gemini was supposed to answer the pre-flight check.

Search API errors blocked two local news items

Brave search returned 400 errors for two queries: a B.C. forestry tariff timeline and the Cariboo Memorial Recreation Complex reopening date. Both requests hit the same endpoint fault. The pipeline proceeded without them. The roundup dropped 52 items total; these two represent a known source of that loss, but the facts do not separate them from other culled content.

TTS retry loop trapped 13 short segments

Sixteen short segments entered text-to-speech synthesis. Thirteen failed on first attempt and exhausted the retry budget. The pipeline did not produce alternative audio for them. Nine segments survived to the final episode.

Three deep dives and one structural question

The episode included three deep dives: housing market bifurcation (Fast Company), Cuba's healthcare collapse (Vox), and diversity in the 2026 NCARB candidate pool (ArchDaily). The debate question examined how Indigenous governance models sustain accountability differently than corporate structures.

Script length ranged from 2707 to 3400 words. One quality score hit 0.84; another measured 0. The citation alignment distribution was 7, 15, 1, 3—uneven across segments.

Two successful runs, a third in progress

The primary run at 1:05 AM Pacific completed 44 minutes late. Fallback 1 launched at 2:05 AM and finished 29 minutes late. Fallback 2 started at 3:05 AM and remained in progress at review time, 32 minutes behind schedule.

Script generation consumed 1153 seconds. Audio rendering took 329 seconds. Deployment and YouTube upload together used 390 seconds. All six pipeline steps reported success in the primary run.

Output metrics

The episode generated 205 RSS entries. Video output was 55.4 minutes long and 19.5 minutes in the audio mix—a discrepancy in the source data. Total spend recorded as $88,037 with the Claude allocation noted separately.
